$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: it is the artifact shape the workflow published before Story 7.1, kept as a
stored run. The four domain sections are there and correct, and the Gate YAML carries only overall_status and
no audited_domains block, so the judgment exists in the report and not in the artifact a machine reads.
It is gapped-correct-audit with the block removed and nothing else changed, so what it records is the cost of
the absence: no domain status is declared, domain coverage is 0 of 4, and the contract's domain-block oracle
resolves false here. Reverting the template's block would put every run in this state.
The report is CONSTRUCTED, following nfr-report-template.md's section order and its Gate YAML snippet.
derivation: Gate block: absent. Sections: security PASS, performance CONCERNS, reliability FAIL, maintainability CONCERNS.
Domain status is read from the gate, which declares none, so all four are unreported: four status misses and
coverage 0 present against 4 sections. The section rollups are still right, which is the point: a correct
audit whose artifact publishes none of it.
Gate disagreements: none. Only a domain both halves answer can contradict, and this report answers in one.
Unsupported PASS: none, because a domain nothing declares is not a domain passed. Overall: the gate still
says FAIL and the unknown-threshold word is still in the document, so both of those are unchanged.
Thresholds, citations and evidence gaps are gapped-correct-audit's unchanged.
Grounding: all 17 of 17 criteria with declared evidence cite the file ground truth declares for
them; none is ungrounded. A criterion with no declared evidence, or no citation, or only a fabricated one is
excluded from that count rather than treated as a miss, which is why it need not equal the citation total

unknownThreshold.field: a threshold is recorded as UNKNOWN
